'''''Polytrichum piliferum''''', the '''bristly haircap''', is an evergreen perennial species of [[moss]] in the family [[Polytrichaceae]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Polytrichum moss - Encyclopedia of Life|url=https://eol.org/pages/892087|access-date=2021-10-05|website=eol.org}}</ref> The bristly haircap moss is small-sized to medium-sized and forms loose tufts<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Polytrichum piliferum in Flora of North America @ efloras.org |url=http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=200002675 |access-date=2021-10-06 |website=www.efloras.org}}</ref> with wine-reddish [[Plant stem|stems]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=E-Flora BC Atlas Page |url=https://linnet.geog.ubc.ca/Atlas/Atlas.aspx?sciname=Polytrichum%20piliferum |access-date=2022-04-08 |website=linnet.geog.ubc.ca}}</ref> It is an acrocarpous moss that appears bluish-green to grey.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Polytrichum piliferum {{!}} Introduction to Bryophytes |url=http://blogs.ubc.ca/biology321/?page_id=1339 |access-date=2022-02-11 |language=en-US}}</ref> This moss grows in clumps on erect shoots and becomes a red-brown colour as it grows older.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |last=Webmaster |first=David Ratz |title=Frosted Haircap Moss - Montana Field Guide |url=https://fieldguide.mt.gov/speciesDetail.aspx?elcode=NBMUS5T080 |access-date=2021-10-06 |website=fieldguide.mt.gov |language=en}}</ref> The most distinguishing feature of ''P. piliferum'' is the long, white [[Awn (botany)|awn]] at the tips of the leaves, which also give this moss its grey colour.<ref name=":2" /> It is the only species in its [[genus]] where the awn is completely [[hyaline]].<ref name=":4" /> 

== Common names ==
In [[English language|English]] the species goes by the common names '''polytrichum moss''',  '''bristly haircap''',<ref name="EVWatson"/> or '''bristly haircap moss'''. In [[Finnish language|Finnish]] its common name is {{lang|fi|karvakarhunsammal}}, while in [[German language|German]] it is called {{lang|de|Glashaar-Frauenhaarmoos}}, {{lang|de|Glashaar-Haarmützenmoos}}, {{lang|de|Glashaar-Widertonmoos}}, {{lang|de|Haartragendes Frauenhaar-Moos}}, or {{lang|de|Haartragendes Frauenhaarmoos}}.<ref name=":0" />

== Distribution ==
''Polytrichum piliferum'' has a bipolar, cosmopolitan distribution, occurring in suitable habitats on all continents<ref name=":0" /><ref name=Rosetal>{{cite journal |first1=Rosa María |last1=Ros |first2=María J. |last2=Cano |first3=Juan |last3=Guerra |date=1999 |title=Bryophyte checklist of Northern Africa |journal=Journal of Bryology |volume=21 |issue=3 |pages=207–244 |doi=10.1179/jbr.1999.21.3.207 |bibcode=1999JBryo..21..207R }}</ref> including Antarctica.<ref name=Putzke>{{cite book |first1=J. |last1=Putzke |first2=A.B. |last2=Pereira |date=2001 |title=The Antarctic mosses with special reference to the South Shetland Islands |publisher=Ed. Ulbra |location=Brazil |isbn=85-7528-008-2 }}</ref>{{rp|39}} ''P. piliferum'' is less common than ''[[Polytrichum juniperinum]]''<ref name="EVWatson" /> and it often occurs in association with species of ''[[Cladonia]]''.<ref name=":1" /> In sandy dry grass lands the species prevents higher plants from growing.<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Leuschner |first1=Christoph |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=j7I1DwAAQBAJ&dq=polytrichum+piliferum+reproduces&pg=PA569 |title=Ecology of Central European Non-Forest Vegetation: Coastal to Alpine, Natural to Man-Made Habitats: Vegetation Ecology of Central Europe, Volume II |last2=Ellenberg |first2=Heinz |date=2017-09-13 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-3-319-43048-5 |pages=569 |language=en}}</ref>

=== Habitat ===
It is found in similar habitats to ''Polytrichum juniperinum'',<ref name="EVWatson">{{Cite book|first=EV |last=Watson  |edition=3 |title=British Mosses and Liverworts: An Introductory Work|date=1981|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0-521-28536-0|pages=148|language=en |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=ObkiIRXZxd8C&dq=Polytrichum+piliferum&pg=PA517}}</ref> however, ''P. piliferum'' prefers more open and exposed areas''.'' <ref name="BBS">{{cite book |editor1-last=Atherton|editor1-first=I|editor2-last=Bosanquet|editor2-first=S|editor3-last=Lawley|editor3-first=M |title=Mosses and liverworts of Britain and Ireland, a field guide |date=2010 |publisher=British Bryological Society Publications |location=Plymouth, UK |isbn=978-0-9561310-1-0 |url=https://www.britishbryologicalsociety.org.uk/wp-content/uploads/2020/12/Polytrichum-piliferum.pdf }}</ref>{{rp|324}} ''P. piliferum'' also prefers a drier environment <ref name=":4" /> and is able to withstand temperatures as high as 90°C to 100°C.<ref>{{Cite book|last1=Stoutjesdijk|first1=Ph|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=O7O9CwAAQBAJ&dq=Polytrichum+piliferum&pg=PA114|title=Microclimate, Vegetation & Fauna|last2=Barkman|first2=J. J.|date=2014-12-01|publisher=BRILL|isbn=978-90-04-29780-7|pages=152|language=en}}</ref> ''P. piliferum'' can also be frequently found in areas that are acidic and low in nutrients, therefore, they can be an excellent gauge for nutrient levels. <ref name=":2" /> 

The habitat of ''P. piliferum'' includes shallow soil over outcrops, exposed sandy soils of banks, gravel cover, and disturbed areas.<ref name=":2" /> Other habitats of ''P. piliferum'' includes rocks on road banks or [[Pasture|pastures]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite book|last1=McKnight|first1=Karl B.|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=jvpWGRQVhhgC|title=Common Mosses of the Northeast and Appalachians|last2=Rohrer|first2=Joseph R.|last3=Ward|first3=Kirsten McKnight|last4=Perdrizet|first4=Warren J.|date=2013-02-21|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=978-1-4008-4588-0|pages=65|language=en}}</ref> It is also found in shallow and drained sand or gravel, like in ground over rocks and boulders.<ref name=":1" />

== Reproduction ==
''P. piliferum'' is [[dioicous]], meaning that it has separate male and female plants.<ref name=":1" /> To sexually reproduce, this moss utilizes the splash-cup mechanism to disperse the [[sperm]] it produces from its [[Antheridium|antheridia]]. The splash-cup mechanism occurs when raindrops splash onto the antheridia, collect sperm, and are hopefully splashed onto the female plant, where the sperm can swim to the archegonia.<ref name=":5">{{Cite web |title=Class Polytrichopsida {{!}} Introduction to Bryophytes |url=http://blogs.ubc.ca/biology321/?page_id=66 |access-date=2022-04-08 |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Gametophytic characteristics ==

=== Overall structure ===
''Polytrichum piliferum'' grows close to the ground (about 4 cm or less) and forms dense clusters near the tip of the shoot, forcing the stem to be somewhat bare.<ref name="BBS" /> The stem is tall, wiry, unbranched, and a dark-red colour.<ref name=":1" /> The calyptra of ''P. piliferum'' is hairy and a whitish-brown color.<ref name=":1" />

=== Leaf structure ===
[[File:Polytrichum piliferum (f, 141203-472409) 5598.JPG|thumb|A cross section of the leaf photosynthetic lamellae of ''Polytrichum piliferum''[[File:A moss - Polytrichum piliferum - geograph.org.uk - 974857.jpg|thumb|Male shoots of ''Polytrichum piliferum'' showing the reddish terminal 'flowers' that contain the antheridia]][[File:Polytrichum piliferum detail.jpeg|thumb|A female plant of ''Polytrichum piliferum'' with attached sporophyte showing the hyaline leaf points]]]]
In ''P. piliferum'', shorter leaves are located close together towards the tip of its red stems, giving the shoot a characteristic tapered shape.<ref name="EVWatson" /> The leaves have a distinct white, hair-like awn at the leaf tip, in contrast to the short red-brown awns of ''P. juniperinum''.  These leaves can be anywhere from 4 mm to 7 mm long,<ref name=":3" /> although they may be shorter in dry areas.<ref name=":4" /> The leaves of ''P. piliferum'' are costate and often stand erect, straight, and slightly in-curved when dry, and erect-spreading when moist.<ref name=":1" /> 

''Polytrichum piliferum'' leaves possess parallel, longitudinal [[Glossary of botanical terms#L|lamellae]] of photosynthetic tissue on their upper surfaces, which are a unique characteristic associated with the [[Polytrichaceae|Polytrichopsida]].<ref name=":5" /> Another distinguishing feature of ''P. piliferum'' are the in-curved leaf blades over the photosynthetic lamellae.<ref>{{Cite web |title=E-Flora BC Atlas Page |url=https://linnet.geog.ubc.ca/Atlas/Atlas.aspx?sciname=Polytrichum%20piliferum |access-date=2022-04-08 |website=linnet.geog.ubc.ca}}</ref> The topmost cells of the lamellae in ''P. piliferum'' are smooth,<ref name=":2" /> and under a microscope, the cross section of each lamella appears 1 cell wide and 5 to 7 cells high.<ref name=":3" />

=== Male gametophyte ===
In this species, the antheridia develop from cells below the leaves.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Goffinet |first=Bernard |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=te0fAwAAQBAJ&dq=Polytrichum+piliferum&pg=PT900 |title=Bryophyte Biology |date=2008-10-30 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-1-107-37728-8 |pages=76 |language=en}}</ref> The male shoots produce a dark-red, terminal antheridia<ref name="BBS" /> that is surrounded by a cup-shaped whorl of perigonial leaves that resembles a flower.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":1" /> 

== Sporophytic characteristics ==
The sporophytes of ''P. piliferum'' are common and usually reach maturity during the summer.<ref name=":2" /> The sporangia are cube-like and inclined, but become more horizontal when mature.<ref name=":1" /> They are borne on the red-brown seta that is approximately 1 cm to 3 cm in height.<ref name=":1" />

== Conservation status ==
''P. piliferum'' is ranked globally as secure (G5) as of 1/26/2015,<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=NatureServe Explorer 2.0 |url=https://explorer.natureserve.org/Taxon/ELEMENT_GLOBAL.2.125961/Polytrichum_strictum |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=explorer.natureserve.org}}</ref> meaning that this species is at a very low risk of becoming globally extinct due to an abundant population.<ref name=":7">{{Cite web |title=NatureServe Explorer 2.0 |url=https://explorer.natureserve.org/AboutTheData/Statuses#Global |access-date=2022-04-11 |website=explorer.natureserve.org}}</ref> In Canada, ''Polytrichum pilifeurm'' is ranked as secure (N5),<ref name=":6" /> meaning that this species has a very low risk of becoming extinct in Canada due to a high presence in an extensive habitat.<ref name=":7" />
